Classification Metrics of Fitted Models

Source: R/classificationMetrics.R
classification-metrics.Rd

Methods of the classification metrics of DescToolsX for fitted models: the confusion matrix (DescToolsX::confusion()), the C-statistic (DescToolsX::cStat()), the Brier score (DescToolsX::brierScore()), the average precision (DescToolsX::averagePrecision()) and the log loss (DescToolsX::logLoss()). The metrics themselves work on predictions and observed outcomes; the methods here take both from a model.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'FitMod'
confusion(x, newdata = NULL, cutoff = 0.5, pos = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'FitMod'
cStat(x, newdata = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'FitMod'
brierScore(x, newdata = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'FitMod'
averagePrecision(x, newdata = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'FitMod'
logLoss(x, newdata = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'glm'
confusion(x, cutoff = 0.5, pos = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'glm'
cStat(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'glm'
brierScore(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'glm'
averagePrecision(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'glm'
logLoss(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multinom'
confusion(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rpart'
confusion(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'randomForest'
confusion(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'svm'
confusion(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lda'
confusion(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'qda'
confusion(x, ...)

Arguments

x

a classification model fitted with fitMod(), or a model object of one of the classes listed under Details

newdata

an optional data frame to evaluate, containing the response. NULL (default) uses the training data. For models fitted with fitMod() only.

cutoff

the probability of the positive class above which an observation is classified as positive, for binary models. Default 0.5.

pos

the positive class of a binary model, by default the second level of the response

...

further arguments passed to the metric, e.g. conf.level, sides, scaled or eps

Value

As the respective metric in DescToolsX.

Details

Models fitted with fitMod(). Predictions come from predict.FitMod(), so the methods work alike for every classification engine (logistic and Firth logistic regression, multinomial models, trees, random forests, ...), on the training data or on newdata. The observed classes are aligned with the probability columns by their labels, so a 0/1 coded response gives the classes "0" and "1", and the second class is the positive one. A binary model is classified by comparing the probability of the positive class with cutoff, a model with more classes by the class of highest probability. The C-statistic, the Brier score, the average precision and the log loss need a binary model.

Other model objects. confusion() has methods for glm, multinom (nnet), rpart, randomForest (out-of-bag predictions), svm (e1071), lda and qda (MASS); cStat(), brierScore(), averagePrecision() and logLoss() have methods for binomial glm objects. These use the fitted values and the response stored in the model. logLoss() additionally requires ungrouped data (all prior weights 1) and refuses quasibinomial, which has no full likelihood.

Measures on the training data are optimistic; crossVal() reports their cross-validated values.

See also

crossVal() for cross-validated metrics, regression-metrics

Other modelling: fitMod(), logitFirth, plot.FitMod(), predict.FitMod(), predictors(), print.FitMod(), regression-metrics

Examples

fit <- fitMod(admit ~ gre + gpa + rank, Admit, engine = "logit")

confusion(fit)
#> 
#> Confusion Matrix and Statistics
#> 
#>           Reference
#> Prediction   1   0
#>          1  30  19
#>          0  97 254
#> 
#>                 Total n : 400
#>                Accuracy : 0.7100
#>                 95% CI : (0.6637, 0.7523)
#>     No Information Rate : 0.6825
#>     P-Value [Acc > NIR] : 0.129
#>                   Kappa : 0.1994
#>  McNemar's Test P-Value : < 0.001
#> 
#>             Sensitivity : 0.2362
#>             Specificity : 0.9304
#>          Pos Pred Value : 0.6122
#>          Neg Pred Value : 0.7236
#>              Prevalence : 0.3175
#>          Detection Rate : 0.0750
#>    Detection Prevalence : 0.1225
#>       Balanced Accuracy : 0.5833
#>                 F-Value : 0.3409
#>     Matthews Cor.-Coef. : 0.2366
#> 
#>        'Positive' Class : 1
#> 
confusion(fit, cutoff = 0.3)
#> 
#> Confusion Matrix and Statistics
#> 
#>           Reference
#> Prediction   1   0
#>          1  85 112
#>          0  42 161
#> 
#>                 Total n : 400
#>                Accuracy : 0.6150
#>                 95% CI : (0.5664, 0.6614)
#>     No Information Rate : 0.6825
#>     P-Value [Acc > NIR] : 0.998
#>                   Kappa : 0.2258
#>  McNemar's Test P-Value : < 0.001
#> 
#>             Sensitivity : 0.6693
#>             Specificity : 0.5897
#>          Pos Pred Value : 0.4315
#>          Neg Pred Value : 0.7931
#>              Prevalence : 0.3175
#>          Detection Rate : 0.2125
#>    Detection Prevalence : 0.4925
#>       Balanced Accuracy : 0.6295
#>                 F-Value : 0.5247
#>     Matthews Cor.-Coef. : 0.2412
#> 
#>        'Positive' Class : 1
#> 
cStat(fit)
#> [1] 0.6928413
brierScore(fit, scaled = TRUE)
#> [1] 0.1014325
averagePrecision(fit)
#> [1] 0.5127557
logLoss(fit)
#> [1] 0.5731469

# out of sample
set.seed(1)
d <- splitTrainTest(Admit, p = 0.3)
m <- update(fit, data = d$train)
confusion(m, newdata = d$test)

#>  McNemar's Test P-Value : 0.015
#> 
#>             Sensitivity : 0.3143
#>             Specificity : 0.8941
#>          Pos Pred Value : 0.5500

#>                 F-Value : 0.4000

#> 
#>        'Positive' Class : 1
#> 
cStat(m, newdata = d$test, conf.level = 0.95)

#> 0.6836975 0.5703704 0.7837733
